[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Advanced Tuning: HalvingGridSearch and HalvingRandomSearch"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Hyperparameter optimization is a crucial step in building high-performing machine learning models. Traditional methods like GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV evaluate every candidate configuration over the entire training dataset. When dealing with large datasets or complex models, this exhaustive approach becomes computationally expensive. Scikit-learn provides successive halving algorithms, namely HalvingGridSearchCV and HalvingRandomSearch, to address this bottleneck efficiently."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Successive Halving"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Successive halving is an iterative selection process. It starts by evaluating all candidate hyperparameter combinations on a small subset of the training data. Based on their performance, only a fraction of the best-performing candidates are promoted to the next iteration, where they are trained on a larger subset of data. This process repeats until a final set of candidates is evaluated on the full dataset."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Resource allocation: Instead of allocating maximum resources (samples) to all candidates, poor configurations are discarded early using fewer resources."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Exploration vs Exploitation: HalvingGridSearch systematically searches the grid, while HalvingRandomSearch samples a subset of candidates randomly, making it ideal for larger search spaces."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing HalvingGridSearchCV"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"The following code demonstrates how to set up and run a HalvingGridSearchCV using a Support Vector Classifier. Note that you must import these modules from the experimental experimental module in scikit-learn."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.svm import SVC
from sklearn.experimental import enable_halving_search_cv
from sklearn.model_selection import HalvingGridSearchCV

X, y = make_classification(n_samples=2000, n_features=20, random_state=42)

param_grid = {
    'C': [0.1, 1, 10, 100],
    'gamma': ['scale', 'auto', 0.01, 0.1]
}

base_estimator = SVC(random_state=42)

sh_grid = HalvingGridSearchCV(
    estimator=base_estimator,
    param_grid=param_grid,
    factor=3,
    resource='n_samples',
    min_resources=100,
    max_resources='auto',
    random_state=42
)

sh_grid.fit(X, y)
print("Best Parameters:", sh_grid.best_params_)"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing HalvingRandomSearchCV"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"When the hyperparameter search space is extremely large, HalvingRandomSearch is preferred over HalvingGridSearch. It randomly samples a specified number of candidate configurations in the first iteration, and then applies the successive halving strategy."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"from scipy.stats import loguniform
from sklearn.model_selection import HalvingRandomSearchCV

param_dist = {
    'C': loguniform(1e-2, 1e2),
    'gamma': loguniform(1e-4, 1e1)
}

sh_random = HalvingRandomSearchCV(
    estimator=base_estimator,
    param_distributions=param_dist,
    n_candidates=30,
    factor=3,
    resource='n_samples',
    min_resources=100,
    random_state=42
)

sh_random.fit(X, y)
print("Best Parameters (Random):", sh_random.best_params_)"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Parameters Explained"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"factor: The proportion of candidates that are selected for the next iteration. A factor of 3 means only 1/3 of the top candidates survive."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"resource: The resource used to measure training effort. Usually set to 'n_samples' (number of training samples), but can also be set to an estimator-specific parameter like 'n_estimators' for random forests."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"min_resources: The amount of resource allocated to each candidate in the first iteration. Ensuring this is sufficiently large is crucial for stable initial evaluations."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"HalvingGridSearchCV and HalvingRandomSearch are powerful tools in scikit-learn for optimizing hyperparameters rapidly without sacrificing model performance. By discarding suboptimal candidates early, they save substantial training time and allow data scientists to explore broader search spaces."}]
